neighbours.label: the whaling trade: whalers, whaling ships and the hunt for whales for oil (including Moby-Dick's Pequod and Nantucket); whale watching, whales as animals, and other fisheries stay low
fire: New Bedford grew rich on whaling in the 1840s.
The whaleship stayed at sea for three years.
Harpooners stood in the bow of the open boat.
Whale oil lit the lamps of Europe.
Crews boiled blubber in try-pots on deck.
The whaler's log records every sperm whale sighted.
Young men from Nantucket shipped out on whalers at fifteen.
quiet: New Bedford grew rich on textiles in the 1890s.
The cargo ship stayed at sea for three weeks.
Fishermen stood in the bow of the open boat.
Olive oil lit the lamps of ancient Rome.
Crews boiled lobsters in pots on deck.
Commercial cod fishing was limited in 1992.
The ranger's log records every grey whale seen from the cliff.
Young men from Nantucket joined the coast guard at eighteen.
